A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIFFINITY, with the same authors, method, and core benchmarks. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original constraint-satisfaction, perplexity, fluency, guidance-scale, and runtime experiments, plus the distribution-preservation experiment in Appendix G.1.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds discrete-diffusion and classifier-guidance comparisons, JSON padding experiments, and analysis of unsuccessful samples.

M1.justification: The guided denoising update, tokenizer–automaton alignment, acceptance-probability algorithm, and final decoding procedure remain unchanged. The revised decoder explanation and stronger probabilistic justification do not establish an altered DIFFINITY procedure.

E1.justification: The 70 JSON schemas and 110 natural-language constraints are retained. Appendix H adds limited JSON test scenarios requiring EOS immediately after the schema, optionally throughout the remaining sequence, extending the original arbitrary-padding requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds LLaDA-8B with DINGO to both benchmark comparisons and evaluates three learned classifier-guidance variants in Section 4.3. GPT2-Small, Medium, Large, and native PLAID guidance remain evaluated; displaced GPT2 table entries are retained in Appendix H.

E3.justification: New classifier experiments introduce three input configurations, balanced positive/negative training pools, roughly 240,000 training pairs, checkpoint selection, and guidance scale 2.5. Additional analyses evaluate unsuccessful and aggregate outputs alongside successful samples. The runtime comparison expands from 14 to 20 benchmarks; original sequence lengths, sampling budgets, and main quality metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds classifier-input ablations, sensitivity to JSON padding/EOS requirements, and quality analysis separating matching from non-matching outputs, including degenerate word-length failures. These substantially extend the retained guidance-scale and distribution-preservation analyses; the latter moves from Appendix G.1 to I.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. New classifier AUC values and subgroup averages are additional point results, not new uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Original DIFFINITY/GPT2 benchmark scores are retained. New results include LLaDA+DINGO's 63.3% JSON satisfaction and 100% pass@10, classifier guidance's 0% JSON satisfaction, and EOS-variant satisfaction rates of 56.8% and 33.6% versus 68.4% with arbitrary padding. Table 5 adds failed-sample and aggregate quality scores. The smallest-automaton latency report changes from 145.6 to 73.6 seconds; the PDFs do not establish this as a controlled same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 changes Equation 4 from an approximation to an exact identity, introduces a conditional-probability integral, and removes the qualification that convergence depends on the unigram approximation. This substantially strengthens the central mathematical justification. The automaton theorems and Appendix E proofs remain unchanged and do not supply a new derivation of that identity.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: training-free guidance for continuous diffusion, targeting syntactically conditioned generation, and favorable validity–quality trade-offs. Added comparisons support these retained claims; the new repository announcement concerns access.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of classifier-score improvement without constraint satisfaction, LLaDA+DINGO's quality degradation, EOS sensitivity attributed to rare EOS generation, and degenerate unsuccessful samples. It expands memory-scaling limitations and removes the earlier batching-saturation explanation. Section 3.3 also removes the explicit high-noise approximation caveat.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a DIFFINITY repository link and adds Appendix F detailing classifier parameter counts, inputs, frozen-backbone gradients, training-data construction, noising, and checkpoint selection. The runtime discussion adds matrix-storage details but deletes the explicit torch.autograd disclosure. Existing hardware, checkpoint, and fluency-prompt appendices are unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged. Section 5 adds a specific proposed extension to length-bounded context-free constraints using the already cited Mündler et al. work, modestly extending the research positioning. The existing discussion of discrete constrained decoding is otherwise retained and relocated.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the decoder, conditioning, baseline, padding, and overhead discussions, introduces a classifier-comparison subsection, and reorganizes the later appendices. It also adds acknowledgments and conference publication text. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main comparison tables are reorganized around new comparator groups, and separate appendix satisfaction/quality tables are consolidated. New displays cover classifier guidance, padding variants, and matching versus non-matching quality. Figure 2c is redrawn with revised data, vertical scale, and legend placement; Figure 1 and Figures 2a–b are retained.

improvement.justification: The added baselines, EOS sensitivity tests, failed-sample analysis, and implementation information address meaningful gaps in v1. However, Section 3.3 replaces a qualified unigram approximation with an exact conditioning identity and removes the convergence qualification without a corresponding derivation; the unchanged appendix proofs establish automaton acceptance calculations only. These empirical and reproducibility gains coexist with weakened support for a central theoretical assertion, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
